placements.why: This envelope's content is a database/platform decision for an analytics pipeline — a technical infrastructure category. No strata exist yet in this repo (EXISTING STRATA is empty), so nothing EXACT or INSPIRED is available to attach to; this is the NEW case where the content itself calls a top-level organizational category into being. 'Architecture' is the canonical name in the org's known taxonomy for exactly this kind of technical-decision content, so it is minted standalone with no parent required.

placements.frame: What capability or performance gain is invoked to justify choosing this platform over the prior one, and does the justification stay quantitative or shift register over time?
placements.why: src-1 declares the Zypherion adoption as settled fact, src-2 supplies the columnar-query performance figure that justifies it, and src-4's bulleted recap re-states both. Per the grain test, the '15x faster' figure is a proof point, not its own leaf — it joins the support of the broader adoption theme it evidences. This names a subject future envelopes will keep feeding (further platform comparisons, performance follow-ups, adoption outcomes), not a one-time fact, so it is leaf-grain. No existing narrative leaf exists in this repo to reuse (EXISTING GRAPH STRUCTURE is empty), so this is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture strata, which exactly covers a technical platform decision.

src-3 pins a concrete start ('next quarter') and src-4's recap restates it as 'Migration starts Q3 2026' — a scheduling commitment distinct from the platform-choice rationale itself, and one future envelopes about this same migration are likely to keep feeding (delays, phase completions, revised dates). It is related to but not identical to the adoption-justification theme, so it is minted as its own leaf under the same Architecture strata, with a 'see' lineage back to the adoption leaf it accompanies rather than being folded into it.
